expectations.text: Includes all named in-boundary components: the web application, PostgreSQL database, and Redis cache, hosted in AWS GovCloud
expectations.evidence: Section 7.1 table lists 'Web application tier', 'PostgreSQL database', 'Redis cache' all marked 'In boundary', under 'AWS GovCloud infrastructure (compute, network, storage)'.

expectations.text: Treats Okta and SendGrid as external services/interconnections: identifies that federal data or metadata flows to them and that their FedRAMP authorization status must be verified and documented
expectations.evidence: Section 7.3 External Connections Table lists Okta and SendGrid with 'FedRAMP Status' column marked '[Confirm: Okta's FedRAMP-authorized offering...]' / '[Confirm: FedRAMP authorization status of SendGrid instance used]', plus action items to confirm authorization status and document ISAs.

expectations.text: Mentions inherited controls / leveraged authorization from AWS GovCloud (e.g., physical and environmental controls inherited, documented via CRM/CIS)
expectations.evidence: Section 7.6 Inherited Controls: 'a substantial share of Physical & Environmental (PE) controls and select System & Communications Protection (SC) controls are inherited. Document the specific inherited controls ... in the CIS/CRM workbook (SSP Appendix I).'

expectations.text: References the requirement for an authorization boundary diagram and data flow diagram consistent with FedRAMP SSP requirements
expectations.evidence: Section 7.2: '[Embed network architecture diagram here.]'; Section 7.3: '[Embed data flow diagram here, showing federal data entering, moving through, and leaving the boundary.]'

expectations.text: Written as usable SSP content: clearly describes what is inside vs outside the boundary and addresses connection security for the external integrations (ports/protocols/TLS, API connections)
